{"parentUuid":"7e8e5774-af16-4215-891f-22d525c81482","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"37408ab2-ab56-4445-8ed4-b7cc28962efb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018VEvF2xfdJSdTbGhafhfSV","type":"tool_result","content":"# Mini-Project #2 — Build a Web CMS with Claude Code\n\n**Course:** IPHS 400 — Frontiers in AI, Kenyon College\n**Instructor:** Jon A. Chun · **Date:** 2026-09-22 · **Weeks 5–6**\n**Format:** Self-guided lab manual. Work at your own pace between class meetings.\n\n---\n\n## Front matter\n\n### What you are building\n\nA content management system: the kind of software WordPress and Drupal are. An **admin console** where you log in, write posts and pages, manage users, and publish; and a **public website** generated from what you published.\n\nThe admin console runs on **your laptop only**. The public site is exported as plain HTML and published to **GitHub Pages**. You will not write the CMS by hand. You will drive Claude Code through a professional workflow — interview, spec, tickets, test-first implementation, code review — and the code will come out of that pipeline.\n\n### Time and deadlines\n\n| Stage | What is due | When (Eastern, EDT) |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Stage 1 — MVP** | Planning artifacts + first 3 tickets, deployed, tagged `mp2-mvp` | Soft target **Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm** |\n| **Stage 2 — Full CMS** | All 7 capabilities, tagged `mp2-final`, report emailed | **Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm**, no-penalty grace to **Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm** |\n\nStage 1 is a *soft* target: its 15 points count as long as the tag exists before the Stage 2 deadline. But you only get feedback in time to use it if you submit on time.\n\n| Part | Topic | Time |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | Overview | 20 min |\n| 1 | Setup: template, skills, first green test | 45 min |\n| 2 | See a real CMS (WordPress Playground) | 30 min |\n| 3 | Your client brief | 20 min |\n| 4 | Exercise A — context-threshold hook | 30 min |\n| 5 | Exercise B — token budget | 45 min |\n| 6 | The loop: grill → spec → tickets → implement → review | 6–9 hrs |\n| 7 | Publish to GitHub Pages | 30 min |\n| 8 | Submit Stage 1 / Stage 2 | 45 min |\n| 9 | Plan B (only if you run out of usage) | 20 min |\n| | **Total** | **11–14 hours over two weeks** |\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- The setup from `manual_ai-swe-setup-macos-win11`: Ghostty (or Windows Terminal + WSL2), `git`, `gh`, `uv`, VS Code, Chrome, Claude Code.\n- A Claude Pro subscription ($20/month).\n- MP1 finished: you have forked, cloned, committed, and pushed before.\n\n### Learning objectives\n\nBy the end you will be able to:\n\n1. Explain how a CMS separates content, roles, and publishing, using the vocabulary of your own project.\n2. Run the mattpocock AI-SWE pipeline end to end and say what each stage is for.\n3. Write tickets as **tracer bullets**: thin vertical slices through data, route, UI, and tests.\n4. Keep an agent honest across many sessions with `CONTEXT.md`, a spec, `/clear`, `/compact`, and `/handoff`.\n5. Budget a fixed-price plan by measuring your own usage instead of guessing.\n6. Ship a working, secure-by-baseline web application and publish its output.\n\n### Deliverables checklist\n\nTick every line before you submit Stage 2. `scripts/check_submission.py` checks all of them for you.\n\n- [ ] `notes/cms-field-notes.md` — what you noticed inside a real CMS\n- [ ] `CONTEXT.md` — your project's glossary · `docs/adr/` — decisions you cannot easily undo\n- [ ] One GitHub issue labeled `spec`; 7–9 issues labeled `ticket`\n- [ ] A `/code-review` findings comment on every ticket before it closes\n- [ ] `docs/transcripts/` — one file per Claude session · `docs/handoff/` — at least one\n- [ ] `docs/process/compaction-log.md` — written by your hook\n- [ ] `notes/token-budget-plan.md` and `notes/usage-ledger.csv`\n- [ ] `docs/screenshots/` — 6 admin screens × 2 widths\n- [ ] `docs/iphs400_mp2-web-cms_report_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md`\n- [ ] README with *Live URL*, *Run locally*, *Generative AI Use Statement*\n- [ ] Live site at `https://{username}.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/`\n- [ ] Tags `mp2-mvp` and `mp2-final` pushed\n\nGrading: the rubric is `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` in the starter repo you copy. Read it **before** you start, not after. Pass/No-Pass, ≥70 passes, 5% of the course grade.\n\n---\n\n## Part 0 — Overview\n\n### 0.1 Why a CMS\n\nEvery newspaper site, club page, and university department runs on one. A CMS is where three ideas meet that you have not built before:\n\n- **Identity and permission.** Who are you, and what are you allowed to do? An editor writes; only an admin creates users. That difference is enforced in code, or it is not real.\n- **Content as data.** A post is not a file of HTML. It is a row with a title, a slug, a body, a status, an author, and dates. Everything else — the admin list, the public page, the navigation — is generated from those rows.\n- **Draft versus published.** The thing you are editing and the thing the world sees are deliberately not the same.\n\nThis is also the first project in this course where a mistake has consequences beyond ugliness: an access-control bug means a user can do something they should not.\n\n### 0.2 The shape of what you build\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    subgraph laptop[\"YOUR LAPTOP (private)\"]\n        A[\"Admin console<br/>FastAPI + Jinja templates\"] --> DB[(\"SQLite database<br/>users, posts, pages\")]\n        DB --> P[\"cms publish<br/>renders published rows\"]\n    end\n    P --> S[\"site/ — plain HTML\"]\n    S --> GH[\"gh-pages branch\"]\n    GH --> W[\"https://you.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/<br/>(public)\"]\n```\n\nThe admin console never goes on the internet. Nobody can attack a server that is not running, and your database and passwords stay on your machine. Publishing is a one-way door: rows in, static HTML out.\n\n### 0.3 The workflow you are learning\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    R[\"/research<br/>learn the domain\"] --> G[\"/grill-with-docs<br/>interviewed one question at a time<br/>→ CONTEXT.md + ADRs\"]\n    G --> S[\"/to-spec<br/>→ one spec issue\"]\n    S --> T[\"/to-tickets<br/>→ 7-9 ticket issues,<br/>each a vertical slice\"]\n    T --> I[\"/implement #N<br/>drives /tdd: red → green → refactor\"]\n    I --> C[\"/code-review<br/>fresh subagent reviews the diff\"]\n    C --> X[\"findings posted on the issue,<br/>then commit 'Closes #N'\"]\n    X -->|\"/clear, next ticket\"| I\n```\n\nFour rules make this work, and all four are graded:\n\n1. **The spec is the single source of truth.** When code and spec disagree, one of them is wrong, and you decide which — you do not let it slide.\n2. **`CONTEXT.md` is the shared vocabulary.** If you call it a \"bulletin\" and the model calls it a \"post\", you will get two designs.\n3. **One ticket per fresh context.** `/clear` between tickets. Long tickets get `/compact` at a green test.\n4. **The reviewer must not be the author.** `/code-review` runs in a fresh subagent because an agent that just wrote code approves its own work.\n\n### 0.4 What is given, what you build\n\n| The template gives you | You build |\n|---|---|\n| Stack and dependencies: FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, argon2 hashing, Markdown sanitizer | All 7 capabilities |\n| **T00, already done:** a \"hello admin\" page, one passing test, `cms publish` shipping a placeholder to Pages | Your data model, login, roles |\n| Folder layout and test helpers such as `client_as(\"editor\")` | Every route, form, and screen |\n| Two example ADRs, a security checklist, `CLAUDE.md`, hooks, pinned skills, `check_submission.py`, README skeleton | Your own ADRs, spec, tickets, tests |\n\nThe template contains **no CMS features**. That is deliberate: features are what you are being taught to produce.\n\n---\n\n## Part 1 — Setup\n\n**Time: 45 min. Usage cost: under 5% of a window — mostly shell commands.**\n\n### 1.1 Make your repo from the template\n\n1. Open `https://github.com/jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter`.\n2. Click the green **Use this template** button → **Create a new repository**.\n3. Owner: your account. Name: **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** exactly. Visibility: **Public**. Click **Create repository**.\n\n> **Why not Fork?** In MP1, forks got re-parented to a classmate's repo, and \"Sync fork\" pulled *their* commits into people's work. A template copy has no fork network, so this cannot happen. It also arrives with Issues switched on, which forks do not.\n\n### 1.2 Clone and install\n\n```bash\ncd ~/code            # or wherever you keep projects\ngh repo clone <your-username>/iphs400-mp2-cms\ncd iphs400-mp2-cms\nuv sync\n```\n\n**Expected:** `uv` prints a list of installed packages ending with a `Resolved … Installed …` summary.\n**If `gh` says you are not logged in:** run `gh auth login` → GitHub.com → HTTPS → authenticate in the browser.","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"be6ae0ba-4c8d-431b-ada4-95f637b7b9ba","timestamp":"2026-09-28T19:48:27.581Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Mini-Project #2 — Build a Web CMS with Claude Code\n\n**Course:** IPHS 400 — Frontiers in AI, Kenyon College\n**Instructor:** Jon A. {"parentUuid":"0e9b3e95-60ad-46cd-aee8-2949bd936e4a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"37408ab2-ab56-4445-8ed4-b7cc28962efb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KfqiB58Fbwt2y2GsbihPr9","type":"tool_result","content":"261:## Part 3 — Your client\n262-\n263-**Time: 20 min.**\n264-\n265-You are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n266-\n267-### 3.1 Pick a client\n268-\n269-Choose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n270-\n271-**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n272-\n273-> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n274-\n275-If you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n276-\n277-### 3.2 Write the brief\n278-\n279-Create `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n280-\n281-- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n282-- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n283-- What is broken about how they do it now?\n284-- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n285-- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n286-\n287-### 3.3 The required capabilities\n288-\n289-Your CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n290-\n291-1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n292-2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n293-3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n294-4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n295-5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n296-6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n297-7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n298-\n299-**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n300-\n301----\n302-\n303-## Part 4 — Exercise A: the context-threshold hook\n304-\n305-**Time: 30 min.** Full instructions: `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` in your repo. Summary:\n306-\n307-You will finish a `Stop` hook that warns you when your context window crosses 50%, 60%, and 80%, and a `PreCompact` hook that logs every compaction. The status line shows a live meter.\n308-\n309-The rule the meter serves: **`/clear` between short tickets; `/compact` at a green test for long ones**, always with a focus note like\n310-\n311-```text\n312-/compact keep: ticket #5 acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched\n313-```\n314-\n315-Your job is `decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py`; seven tests fail until it works:\n316-\n317-```text\n318-/clear\n319-/tdd Implement decide() in .claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py so the failing tests in tests/test_ctx_guard.py pass. Do not change the tests.\n320-```\n321-\n322-Graded as B6.\n323-\n324----\n325-\n326-## Part 5 — Exercise B: the token budget\n327-\n328-**Time: 45 min.** Graded as B7 (3 pts) and discussed in your report.\n329-\n330-### 5.1 Why you cannot budget in tokens\n331-\n332-Anthropic does not publish a token count for Pro. Usage is metered as a **rolling 5-hour session** plus a **weekly cap across all models**, and what you spend depends on message length, conversation length, attachments, tool use, model, and effort level. So you cannot plan in tokens. {"parentUuid":"22d0023f-0917-4c19-a1a4-920f2951aab6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWRNV8YZG7UWfBriBEN7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Good — Office of Institutional Research (IR) at Kenyon is specific and plausible; that clears Q1. Now the branches that hang off \"who is this for.\"\n\n❓ **Q2** - **Who runs it, and how comfortable are they with computers?**: In a real IR office this is usually a small staff — a director, maybe one or two research analysts, a data/assessment coordinator. Who are the people posting content, and what's their technical comfort level (comfortable with Markdown vs. needs something closer to a Word doc)?\n\n➡️ My recommendation: a Director (admin — approves and publishes final reports, manages accounts) and one or two Analysts (editor — draft survey results, fact books, data briefs, but can't publish without director sign-off or at least can't touch the \"About/Mission\" page).\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3** - **Who reads the public site, and what are they usually hunting for?**: IR offices typically serve Deans/faculty (accreditation and planning data), the Board of Trustees, prospective students' families (Common Data Set, fast facts), and accreditors (self-study reports). Who's your actual audience, and what do they come back for repeatedly?\n\n➡️ My recommendation: faculty/administrators looking for the latest Fact Book and enrollment data, plus accreditors/board members looking for historical reports — i.e., people who want the *current* numbers fast and *past* numbers archived.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4** - **What's broken about how they do it now?**: E.g. reports live as scattered PDFs emailed around, or buried in an old Drupal site nobody can edit without IT, or a Google Drive folder with confusing versioning.\n\n➡️ My recommendation (plausible default): reports currently sit in a shared drive folder with inconsistent naming, so people email IR directly asking \"what's the latest fact book\" instead of finding it themselves.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5** - **What must never happen?**: The hard constraint — something that would be actively bad if it broke, not just annoying. E.g. \"an analyst must never be able to alter or delete a report that's already published and cited elsewhere,\" or \"draft data with unreleased enrollment numbers must never leak to the public site before it's official.\"\n\n➡️ My recommendation: unreleased/draft data (e.g. this term's still-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public site — draft/published separation is the load-bearing constraint, more than role mistakes.\n\nAnswer what you know; where you're guessing at how a real IR office works, just say so and we'll go with something plausible — it only needs to be specific and internally consistent, not accurate to the real Kenyon office."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":71,"cache_read_input_tokens":84643,"output_tokens":1308,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":445},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":71,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1308,"cache_read_input_tokens":84643,"cache_creation_input_tokens":71,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":71},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfWRNTcktoFAnBswdWyt6","type":"assistant","uuid":"8a459463-366a-4658-9f42-c117459146fd","timestamp":"2026-09-28T19:52:31.867Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"ab8fd274-dd85-4f51-8c74-7f71656a432d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"73a0f1b2-e01b-44ee-a6e2-5ddd8e3c9846","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018D5naDN934wB2c2S46FcUj","type":"tool_result","content":"# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. {"parentUuid":"80bff9bc-c47c-43c8-8523-c9537b88f10b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWSC7Jy8Qidcwzt6kRJa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01E8c6Bq4EXTPmeydMic9xhJ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md","content":"# Analysts publish Updates directly; only the Director publishes Reports\n\nAnalysts (including interns) currently email IR staff or drop files in a\nshared OneDrive folder to get anything posted, which is the exact bottleneck\nthis CMS exists to remove. {"parentUuid":"7b39361a-304b-4b5e-9aaf-b183bfba2145","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWSCUi5Syvwh87vT5thE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll also fill in `notes/client-brief.md` since the manual asks for it — drafted from what we settled, worth skimming to make sure it sounds like you."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":563,"cache_read_input_tokens":98568,"output_tokens":1358,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":622},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":563,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1358,"cache_read_input_tokens":98568,"cache_creation_input_tokens":563,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":563},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfWSCUEoaACaWQctfyffx","type":"assistant","uuid":"a8264bb0-1a63-4159-b904-dd8ae4e4d438","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:03:12.963Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"a8264bb0-1a63-4159-b904-dd8ae4e4d438","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWSCUi5Syvwh87vT5thE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019uGkACkbmTbhDjgYk8Q8FM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","content":"# Client brief — Kenyon Office of Institutional Research\n\n**Who runs it, how comfortable are they with computers?** Two people: a\nDirector (modeled on the real office's Associate VP for IR) and\nAnalysts/interns who rotate by semester. Comfortable with spreadsheets and\nWord, not with anything more technical — Markdown with a preview is about the\nceiling.\n\n**Who reads it, what are they after?** Split audience. Internally, faculty\nand administrators come back for the current Factbook and enrollment numbers.\nAccreditors and board members want historical reports for self-studies.\nExternally, some of it — the Factbook, Common Data Set, Data Gallery — is\ngenuinely public, matching what's actually live on kenyon.edu today.\n\n**What's broken now?** Reports live scattered across a shared OneDrive\nfolder with inconsistent naming. Multiple interns work on things at the same\ntime, so it's unclear which version is current, and people end up emailing\nIR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it\nthemselves.\n\n**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** An intern can draft and\npublish a routine Update without emailing a link around. The Director can\nsee everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.\n\n**What must never happen?** Draft or unreleased data (e.g. this term's\nstill-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public\nsite before it's official. Relatedly, a Report that's already published and\ncited elsewhere (Factbook, CDS) must never be editable or publishable by\nanyone but the Director — see [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":563,"cache_read_input_tokens":98568,"output_tokens":1358,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":622},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":563,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1358,"cache_read_input_tokens":98568,"cache_creation_input_tokens":563,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":563},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_019uGkACkbmTbhDjgYk8Q8FM":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","content":"# Client brief — Kenyon Office of Institutional Research\n\n**Who runs it, how comfortable are they with computers?** Two people: a\nDirector (modeled on the real office's Associate VP for IR) and\nAnalysts/interns who rotate by semester. Comfortable with spreadsheets and\nWord, not with anything more technical — Markdown with a preview is about the\nceiling.\n\n**Who reads it, what are they after?** Split audience. Internally, faculty\nand administrators come back for the current Factbook and enrollment numbers.\nAccreditors and board members want historical reports for self-studies.\nExternally, some of it — the Factbook, Common Data Set, Data Gallery — is\ngenuinely public, matching what's actually live on kenyon.edu today.\n\n**What's broken now?** Reports live scattered across a shared OneDrive\nfolder with inconsistent naming. Multiple interns work on things at the same\ntime, so it's unclear which version is current, and people end up emailing\nIR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it\nthemselves.\n\n**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** An intern can draft and\npublish a routine Update without emailing a link around. The Director can\nsee everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.\n\n**What must never happen?** Draft or unreleased data (e.g. this term's\nstill-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public\nsite before it's official. Relatedly, a Report that's already published and\ncited elsewhere (Factbook, CDS) must never be editable or publishable by\nanyone but the Director — see [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md).\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfWSCUEoaACaWQctfyffx","type":"assistant","uuid":"d99a1007-28a1-4032-a919-d46b61382ca7","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:03:18.826Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

Comfortable with spreadsheets and\nWord, not with anything more technical — Markdown with a preview is about the\nceiling.\n\n**Who reads it, what are they after?** Split audience. Internally, faculty\nand administrators come back for the current Factbook and enrollment numbers.\nAccreditors and board members want historical reports for self-studies.\nExternally, some of it — the Factbook, Common Data Set, Data Gallery — is\ngenuinely public, matching what's actually live on kenyon.edu today.\n\n**What's broken now?** Reports live scattered across a shared OneDrive\nfolder with inconsistent naming. Multiple interns work on things at the same\ntime, so it's unclear which version is current, and people end up emailing\nIR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it\nthemselves.\n\n**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** An intern can draft and\npublish a routine Update without emailing a link around. The Director can\nsee everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.\n\n**What must never happen?** Draft or unreleased data (e.g. this term's\nstill-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public\nsite before it's official. Relatedly, a Report that's already published and\ncited elsewhere (Factbook, CDS) must never be editable or publishable by\nanyone but the Director — see [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md).\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d99a1007-28a1-4032-a919-d46b61382ca7","session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article","originalFile":"# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Covers both permanent staff analysts and semester interns.\nCan draft and publish Updates directly; can draft but not publish or edit\nReports.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Update**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (an Update or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":13,"oldLines":16,"newStart":13,"newLines":16,"lines":[" _Avoid_: Admin, superuser"," "," **Analyst**:","-The editor role. Never","originalFile":"# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. A single shared account used by whichever intern is on\nshift that semester — not one account per person. Can draft and publish\nData Bites directly; can draft but not publish or edit Reports.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (an Update or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":31,"oldLines":7,"newStart":31,"newLines":7,"lines":[" _Avoid_: Page, document"," "," **Draft**:","-Content (an Update or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never","+Content (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never"," appears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers"," still being verified before the official count."," _Avoid_: Unpublished, pending"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5290b06e-0e1c-4f63-8d27-492b1c5569f5","session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"3e4b859c-0a68-4df9-904f-b4c57a0d08a5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWSZftryL7vBMLKHJXHc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018PkoLPdaay4G1dxJGk4N3L","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md","content":"# Analysts publish Data Bites directly; only the Director publishes Reports; interns share one Analyst account\n\nAnalysts (interns) currently email IR staff or drop files in a shared\nOneDrive folder to get anything posted, which is the exact bottleneck this\nCMS exists to remove. But Reports (Factbook, Common Data Set, Survey Policy)\nget cited externally and must stay accurate and stable, so we don't want\nintern turnover or a drafting mistake taking one live unreviewed.\n\nWe decided: the editor permission is split by content type, not uniform.\nAnalysts can create, edit, and **publish** a Data Bite without approval.\nAnalysts can create and edit a Report, but only the Director (admin) can\npublish or edit a Report once it exists — even one an Analyst drafted.\n\nWe also decided interns share **one** Analyst account rather than getting\nindividual logins. This was a deliberate simplicity-over-attribution\ntrade-off: with only a couple of interns rotating per semester and Data\nBites being low-stakes, per-intern accounts (and the Director having to\ncreate/deactivate one each semester) weren't worth the overhead. The cost is\nthat a Data Bite's author field says \"Analyst,\" not which specific intern\nwrote it — acceptable here because Reports (the content that's actually\ncited and needs accountability) are still gated to the named Director.\n\nThe alternative (uniform editor rights, or a Director-approves-everything\ngate) was rejected: the former risks an intern accidentally publishing a\nFactbook revision, the latter reintroduces the \"email IR to post something\"\nbottleneck for the routine, low-stakes case.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":285,"cache_read_input_tokens":103501,"output_tokens":648,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":285,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":648,"cache_read_input_tokens":103501,"cache_creation_input_tokens":285,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":285},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_018PkoLPdaay4G1dxJGk4N3L":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md","content":"# Analysts publish Data Bites directly; only the Director publishes Reports; interns share one Analyst account\n\nAnalysts (interns) currently email IR staff or drop files in a shared\nOneDrive folder to get anything posted, which is the exact bottleneck this\nCMS exists to remove. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.","originalFile":"# Client brief — Kenyon Office of Institutional Research\n\n**Who runs it, how comfortable are they with computers?** Two people: a\nDirector (modeled on the real office's Associate VP for IR) and\nAnalysts/interns who rotate by semester. Comfortable with spreadsheets and\nWord, not with anything more technical — Markdown with a preview is about the\nceiling.\n\n**Who reads it, what are they after?** Split audience. Internally, faculty\nand administrators come back for the current Factbook and enrollment numbers.\nAccreditors and board members want historical reports for self-studies.\nExternally, some of it — the Factbook, Common Data Set, Data Gallery — is\ngenuinely public, matching what's actually live on kenyon.edu today.\n\n**What's broken now?** Reports live scattered across a shared OneDrive\nfolder with inconsistent naming. Multiple interns work on things at the same\ntime, so it's unclear which version is current, and people end up emailing\nIR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it\nthemselves.\n\n**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** An intern can draft and\npublish a routine Update without emailing a link around. The Director can\nsee everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.\n\n**What must never happen?** Draft or unreleased data (e.g. this term's\nstill-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public\nsite before it's official. Relatedly, a Report that's already published and\ncited elsewhere (Factbook, CDS) must never be editable or publishable by\nanyone but the Director — see [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":8,"newStart":18,"newLines":9,"lines":[" IR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it"," themselves."," ","-**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** An intern can draft and","-publish a routine Update without emailing a link around. {"parentUuid":"bb36e8b8-b60b-4eb6-be02-eedc8ea5098d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"cf0f383b-24ef-4be7-aea2-309bd15b433d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-spec\n\nThis skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user; just synthesize what you already know.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.\n\nCheck with the user that these seams match their expectations.\n\n3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.\n\n<spec-template>\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.\n\n## Solution\n\nThe solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.\n\n## User Stories\n\nA LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:\n\n1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>\n\n<user-story-example>\n1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending\n</user-story-example>\n\nThis list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\nA list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:\n\n- The modules that will be built/modified\n- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified\n- Technical clarifications from the developer\n- Architectural decisions\n- Schema changes\n- API contracts\n- Specific interactions\n\nDo NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.\n\nException: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA list of testing decisions that were made. Include:\n\n- A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)\n- Which modules will be tested\n- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nA description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.\n\n## Further Notes\n\nAny further notes about the feature.\n\n</spec-template>\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"0b0a35a1-dbc3-4f05-bf43-d82e6c114917","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:09:53.582Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"e3ce719b-69a3-48dd-9bb5-991df7af60fe","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"cf0f383b-24ef-4be7-aea2-309bd15b433d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LuZ4PeVPwuuFQXhJJYSzwR","type":"tool_result","content":"--- conftest ---\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n--- test_t00 ---\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. These pass in the fresh template.\n\nDo not delete them. If a change breaks them, the change broke the app's front\ndoor.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef test_admin_console_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_public_home_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_publish_writes_a_site(tmp_path):\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    out = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\")\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists() and (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_published_html_uses_relative_paths(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Root-absolute paths break on GitHub Pages project URLs (rubric F2).\"\"\"\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    html = (render_site(tmp_path / \"site\") / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert 'href=\"/' not in html and 'src=\"/' not in html\n--- main.py ---\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n--- settings.py ---\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n--- publish.py ---\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n--- cli.py ---\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"5fac17a4-ecea-4880-bed5-9bcaea4860f8","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:10:02.145Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"--- conftest ---\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. {"parentUuid":"2c7f2a6c-c2e0-4d12-9536-39fcd7536184","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"cf0f383b-24ef-4be7-aea2-309bd15b433d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015YsNuK4yXsMwgWWx5AfPT6","type":"tool_result","content":"[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n---ADR001---\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n---ADR002---\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\n---security---\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\n--- gh label {"parentUuid":"d2322fdf-364d-41bd-9728-1ab710c94658","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWSjUAChJHFzXoKMhxMM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"**Testing seam**, before I write the spec: the template already sets one up — `tests/conftest.py`'s `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures hit the FastAPI app through `TestClient` (real HTTP requests, real routes, a real SQLite db). That's the highest, and only, seam I'd use: every ticket's tests go through `client_as(\"director\" | \"analyst\")` making real requests and checking response status/HTML/DB state — no mocking the DB or auth layer separately. Matches \"one seam\" and reuses what's already there.\n\nConfirm that's right, then here's the spec I'll publish as the `spec` issue (this repo uses `spec`/`ticket`/`stretch` labels, not `ready-for-agent` — following `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`):\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor, one shared account for rotating interns) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft and publish Data Bites (short, dated items) without waiting on the Director, but only the Director can publish or edit a Report (durable, cited documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set). `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with the shared Analyst account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As a Director, I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore, without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite I previously published, so that I can fix a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create and edit a Report (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can draft the next Factbook or Common Data Set update.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish a Report I drafted, so that cited documents can't go live without Director review.\n16. As a Director, I want to publish, edit, or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n17. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n18. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing, so that I can see how content will actually render before publishing.\n21. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data.\n22. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n23. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages.\n24. As anyone, I want content and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n25. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n26. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown bodies sanitized before rendering anywhere (admin preview and public export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: `Director` (admin) and `Analyst` (editor) — two enum-like role values on a user record, matching `CONTEXT.md`. No third role.\n- **Content types**: `DataBite` and `Report`, both with title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, created/updated timestamps. Modeled as two tables (or one table with a `kind` discriminant) — implementer's call, exposed no differently at the route/template layer.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts have full CRUD + publish on `DataBite`. Analysts have create/edit but not publish/delete on `Report`. Directors have full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Publish gate**: a content item only reaches `site/` when its status is `published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) is extended to iterate published `DataBite`/`Report` rows instead of the current empty `items=[]` placeholder, writing one file per item plus an index, all with relative paths.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only (Data Bites are not nav items — they're the dated/list content, matching the Update/Report split in `CONTEXT.md`).\n- **Auth**: session-based via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`, already a dependency), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`. Login/logout routes issue and clear the session cookie.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form, validated server-side on POST.\n- **Sanitization**: Markdown bodies run through `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before being stored for preview and before being written to the export, per Security Checklist item 7.\n- **Shared Analyst account**: exactly one Analyst-role user is expected to exist for the demo/seed; the Director-creates-user story still exercises full user CRUD generically (it isn't restricted to \"one Analyst only\" in code — that's an operational choice by the office, not a system constraint).\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no separate unit-testing of the permission logic in isolation. `client_as(\"editor\")` will need updating (or a parallel fixture) once \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" role names exist, since `DEMO_USERS` currently keys on `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"`.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state assertions (e.g., a published item exists in the export) where relevant.\n- Access-control tests are required per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft present, assert it's absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): media uploads, categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric; tickets (`/to-tickets`) will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\n\n---\n\nConfirm the seam and the draft, and I'll publish this as the `spec` issue."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2427,"cache_read_input_tokens":110319,"output_tokens":4382,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1297},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2427,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4382,"cache_read_input_tokens":110319,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2427,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2427},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfWSjThAriYFGk6xZ6skj","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-spec","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"5d20ef7d-6b06-4f00-a7c9-f4f9a8f9f083","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:10:49.210Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}
