{"parentUuid":"95f1414d-de94-4056-8de3-37ede96e9712","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWUAyHDegujC8PYnw1SM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XgcUFPgPMrXjrTKGwTRy2t","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"mkdir -p /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/state && cat /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/state/phase 2>/dev/null; echo \"---\"; cat > /tmp/spec_body.md << 'SPECEOF'\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor, one shared account for rotating interns) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft, edit, publish, and unpublish Data Bites (short, dated items) without waiting on the Director, but only the Director can publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it exists (durable, cited documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set). `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages, with content-type-namespaced paths.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with the shared Analyst account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As any authenticated user (Director or Analyst), I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore — even with a browser tab still holding an old session cookie — without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite (including one another Analyst drafted or published), so that shift changes don't block fixing a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed; Analysts cannot delete Data Bites.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create and edit a **draft** Report (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can draft the next Factbook or Common Data Set update — including one another Analyst started, for shift continuity.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish, edit, or unpublish a Report once it's published, so that cited documents can't be changed or taken down without Director review.\n16. As a Director, I want to publish, edit, or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n17. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n18. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing, so that I can see how content will actually render (post-sanitization) before publishing.\n21. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data.\n22. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n23. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content, writing Data Bites to `data-bites/<slug>.html` and Reports to `reports/<slug>.html` with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages and the two content types never collide.\n24. As an Analyst or Director, I want a duplicate slug within the same content type rejected at save time with a clear error, so that two items can never overwrite each other's export path.\n25. As anyone, I want content and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n26. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form — including login and logout — protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n27. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown bodies stored raw and sanitized only at render time (preview and export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute anywhere it's displayed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: internal role values stay `admin` and `editor` (compatibility with `tests/conftest.py`'s `DEMO_USERS` and `client_as` fixture); templates display them as \"Director\" and \"Analyst\" respectively. No third role.\n- **Content types**: `DataBite` and `Report`, both with title, slug, raw Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`. Editing an item (by any Analyst, for shift continuity) preserves the original author and `created_at`; only `updated_at` changes.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts — full create/edit/publish/unpublish on `DataBite`, no delete. Analysts — create/edit on **draft** `Report` only; once a `Report` is published, only the Director may edit, unpublish, or delete it, and only the Director may ever publish a `Report`. Directors — full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Auth**: every `/admin/*` route requires an authenticated session (redirect to login if anonymous). Every protected request re-validates the session's user as active server-side — a deactivated user's existing signed cookie must fail on the next request, not just on next login. Session via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form and validated server-side on POST, including `/login` and `/logout`.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: raw Markdown is what's stored. Rendering (preview or export) always runs `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before display; pre-rendered/sanitized HTML is never persisted.\n- **Reports are Markdown pages, not files**: a Report is authored the same way as a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body) and rendered to HTML at publish/export time. File/media uploads are out of scope entirely — a Report is not a PDF upload.\n- **Publish gate & export paths**: an item reaches `site/` only when `status == published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) iterates published `DataBite` rows into `data-bites/<slug>.html` and published `Report` rows into `reports/<slug>.html`, plus an index/nav, all with relative paths. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Shared Analyst account**: exactly one Analyst-role user is expected for the demo/seed; the Director-creates-user story still exercises full, generic user CRUD in code — nothing in the system enforces \"only one Analyst,\" that's an office policy choice, not a code constraint.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft present, assert it's absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit, unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Media/file uploads (Reports are Markdown pages, not PDFs). Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric; tickets (`/to-tickets`) will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\nSPECEOF\necho \"written\""},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":490,"cache_read_input_tokens":117128,"output_tokens":5860,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1704},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":490,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5860,"cache_read_input_tokens":117128,"cache_creation_input_tokens":490,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":490},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01XgcUFPgPMrXjrTKGwTRy2t":{"command":"mkdir -p /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/state && cat /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/state/phase 2>/dev/null; echo \"---\"; cat > /tmp/spec_body.md << 'SPECEOF'\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor, one shared account for rotating interns) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft, edit, publish, and unpublish Data Bites (short, dated items) without waiting on the Director, but only the Director can publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it exists (durable, cited documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set). `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages, with content-type-namespaced paths.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with the shared Analyst account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As any authenticated user (Director or Analyst), I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore — even with a browser tab still holding an old session cookie — without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite (including one another Analyst drafted or published), so that shift changes don't block fixing a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed; Analysts cannot delete Data Bites.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create and edit a **draft** Report (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can draft the next Factbook or Common Data Set update — including one another Analyst started, for shift continuity.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish, edit, or unpublish a Report once it's published, so that cited documents can't be changed or taken down without Director review.\n16. As a Director, I want to publish, edit, or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n17. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n18. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing, so that I can see how content will actually render (post-sanitization) before publishing.\n21. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data.\n22. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n23. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content, writing Data Bites to `data-bites/<slug>.html` and Reports to `reports/<slug>.html` with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages and the two content types never collide.\n24. As an Analyst or Director, I want a duplicate slug within the same content type rejected at save time with a clear error, so that two items can never overwrite each other's export path.\n25. As anyone, I want content and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n26. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form — including login and logout — protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n27. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown bodies stored raw and sanitized only at render time (preview and export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute anywhere it's displayed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: internal role values stay `admin` and `editor` (compatibility with `tests/conftest.py`'s `DEMO_USERS` and `client_as` fixture); templates display them as \"Director\" and \"Analyst\" respectively. No third role.\n- **Content types**: `DataBite` and `Report`, both with title, slug, raw Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`. Editing an item (by any Analyst, for shift continuity) preserves the original author and `created_at`; only `updated_at` changes.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts — full create/edit/publish/unpublish on `DataBite`, no delete. Analysts — create/edit on **draft** `Report` only; once a `Report` is published, only the Director may edit, unpublish, or delete it, and only the Director may ever publish a `Report`. Directors — full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Auth**: every `/admin/*` route requires an authenticated session (redirect to login if anonymous). Every protected request re-validates the session's user as active server-side — a deactivated user's existing signed cookie must fail on the next request, not just on next login. Session via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form and validated server-side on POST, including `/login` and `/logout`.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: raw Markdown is what's stored. Rendering (preview or export) always runs `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before display; pre-rendered/sanitized HTML is never persisted.\n- **Reports are Markdown pages, not files**: a Report is authored the same way as a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body) and rendered to HTML at publish/export time. File/media uploads are out of scope entirely — a Report is not a PDF upload.\n- **Publish gate & export paths**: an item reaches `site/` only when `status == published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) iterates published `DataBite` rows into `data-bites/<slug>.html` and published `Report` rows into `reports/<slug>.html`, plus an index/nav, all with relative paths. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Shared Analyst account**: exactly one Analyst-role user is expected for the demo/seed; the Director-creates-user story still exercises full, generic user CRUD in code — nothing in the system enforces \"only one Analyst,\" that's an office policy choice, not a code constraint.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft present, assert it's absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit, unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Media/file uploads (Reports are Markdown pages, not PDFs). Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric; tickets (`/to-tickets`) will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\nSPECEOF\necho \"written\""}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfWUAxkU4gXAexvVYpV4e","type":"assistant","uuid":"8f34b4f3-36c8-47b0-aa50-5a7d09fac3ad","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:29:59.032Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"2b7abafa-c69f-4ebc-baab-2aa4b9f850e2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWUL1Xeq3s9zMppqDy1c","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KFzKmF9pvUhjH2umPYYrcp","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /tmp/spec_body.md << 'SPECEOF'\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor, one shared account for rotating interns) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft, edit, publish, and unpublish Data Bites (short, dated Markdown items) without waiting on the Director. Reports (Factbook, Common Data Set, Survey Policy) are file uploads (matching how these documents actually circulate — real, cite-able PDFs) plus a required short Markdown caption; only the Director can publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it exists. `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages, with content-type-namespaced paths.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with the shared Analyst account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As any authenticated user (Director or Analyst), I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore — even with a browser tab still holding an old session cookie — without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite (including one another Analyst drafted or published), so that shift changes don't block fixing a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed; Analysts cannot delete Data Bites.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create a **draft** Report by uploading a file (e.g. the Factbook PDF) plus a short Markdown caption, so that I can prepare the next cited document.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to edit a draft Report — replace the file, edit the caption — including one another Analyst started, so that shift changes don't block prep work.\n16. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it's published, so that cited documents can't be changed or taken down without Director review.\n17. As a Director, I want to publish, edit (including replacing the file), or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n18. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n21. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing a Data Bite or a Report's caption, so that I can see how it will actually render (post-sanitization) before publishing.\n22. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data, and never a draft's uploaded file.\n23. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n24. As a visitor, I want to download a published Report's file from its page, so that I get the actual cited document.\n25. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content, writing Data Bites to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, Reports to `reports/<slug>.html`, and Report files to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>`, all with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages and nothing collides.\n26. As an Analyst or Director, I want a duplicate slug within the same content type rejected at save time with a clear error, so that two items can never overwrite each other's export path.\n27. As an uploader, I want a Report upload restricted to an allowlisted file type (PDF) and a size cap, so that the upload path can't be used to smuggle arbitrary or oversized files.\n28. As anyone, I want content, files, and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n29. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form — including login and logout — protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n30. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown (Data Bite bodies, Report captions) stored raw and sanitized only at render time (preview and export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute anywhere it's displayed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: internal role values stay `admin` and `editor` (compatibility with `tests/conftest.py`'s `DEMO_USERS` and `client_as` fixture); templates display them as \"Director\" and \"Analyst\" respectively. No third role.\n- **DataBite**: title, slug, raw Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`.\n- **Report**: title, slug, uploaded file (PDF; allowlisted extension + MIME type; size-capped — exact cap is an implementation detail, pick something generous but bounded, e.g. 20MB), a required short raw-Markdown caption, status, author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`. This doubles as the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal.\n- **Shift-continuity editing**: any Analyst may edit an item (Data Bite, or a Report while still draft) regardless of who created or last edited it; the original author and `created_at` are preserved, only `updated_at` changes.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts — full create/edit/publish/unpublish on `DataBite`, no delete. Analysts — create/edit on **draft** `Report` only (including replacing the uploaded file); once a `Report` is published, only the Director may edit, unpublish, or delete it, and only the Director may ever publish one. Directors — full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Auth**: every `/admin/*` route requires an authenticated session (redirect to login if anonymous). Every protected request re-validates the session's user as active server-side — a deactivated user's existing signed cookie must fail on the next request, not just on next login. Session via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form and validated server-side on POST, including `/login` and `/logout`.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: raw Markdown is what's stored (Data Bite bodies, Report captions). Rendering (preview or export) always runs `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before display; pre-rendered/sanitized HTML is never persisted.\n- **File uploads**: handled via the existing `python-multipart` dependency (no new dependency needed). Uploaded files are stored outside `site/` (e.g. a local `uploads/` directory, gitignored like the DB) until publish; a draft Report's file must never appear in `site/`, same rule as draft content generally.\n- **Publish gate & export paths**: an item reaches `site/` only when `status == published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) writes published `DataBite` rows to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, published `Report` rows to `reports/<slug>.html` (rendering the caption + a download link), and copies each published Report's file to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>` — all relative paths. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Shared Analyst account**: exactly one Analyst-role user is expected for the demo/seed; the Director-creates-user story still exercises full, generic user CRUD in code — nothing in the system enforces \"only one Analyst,\" that's an office policy choice, not a code constraint.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload in a Data Bite body and a Report caption, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft Data Bite and a draft Report (with its file) present, assert both are absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Upload-validation test: a non-PDF or oversized file is rejected at upload time with a clear error.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit (including replacing the file), unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003), uploads for Data Bites (Data Bites stay Markdown-only; only Reports carry a file).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric, plus the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal folded into the Report content type. `/to-tickets` will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\nSPECEOF\necho written; wc -l /tmp/spec_body.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1408,"cache_read_input_tokens":123625,"output_tokens":5934,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":1484},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1408,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5934,"cache_read_input_tokens":123625,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1408,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1408},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01KFzKmF9pvUhjH2umPYYrcp":{"command":"cat > /tmp/spec_body.md << 'SPECEOF'\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Shared Analyst account**: exactly one Analyst-role user is expected for the demo/seed; the Director-creates-user story still exercises full, generic user CRUD in code — nothing in the system enforces \"only one Analyst,\" that's an office policy choice, not a code constraint.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload in a Data Bite body and a Report caption, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft Data Bite and a draft Report (with its file) present, assert both are absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Upload-validation test: a non-PDF or oversized file is rejected at upload time with a clear error.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit (including replacing the file), unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003), uploads for Data Bites (Data Bites stay Markdown-only; only Reports carry a file).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric, plus the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal folded into the Report content type. `/to-tickets` will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\nSPECEOF\necho written; wc -l /tmp/spec_body.md"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfWUKziY8CNRhqsLuTTAL","type":"assistant","uuid":"5c531412-db53-476d-97b7-84ff2870df4f","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:31:59.521Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"2797b3bb-7e57-40b4-b4fb-f5b27b1f7920","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7a96ecc6-2e76-4d00-b157-7f0194afa0f2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. {"parentUuid":"cf6f9c4c-20db-4641-a496-acdcf6aba9a3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWUe1F3xHAuXWvpErTuo","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Working from spec #1. Includes the DB layer (users table) — the prefactor everything else needs. |\n| **T02** | User management | T01 | Director creates a user, changes a role, deactivates one; deactivated user can't log in; Analyst can't reach any of this (403/redirect). |\n| **T03** | Data Bites | T01 | Full Data Bite lifecycle: Analyst creates/edits/publishes/unpublishes (no delete), Director deletes, drafts never leak, slug collisions rejected, shift-continuity editing (any Analyst can edit any Data Bite). |\n| **T04** | Reports (draft/publish lockdown) | T01 | Report lifecycle with the asymmetric permission rule: Analyst creates/edits **draft only**; once published, only Director can edit/unpublish/delete/publish. Markdown body required. Slug collisions rejected. |\n| **T05** | Report file attachment | T04 | Optional file upload on a Report (PDF, allowlisted type, size-capped), draft file never in `site/`, published file downloadable, replacing the file follows the same lockdown as T04. |\n| **T06** | Admin console | T03, T04 | Dashboard with real counts, content list filterable by type/status, Markdown preview (sanitized) while editing either content type. |\n| **T07** | Public site & publish | T03, T04 | Public pages for published Data Bites and Reports, nav built from published Reports, `cms publish` exporting to `data-bites/<slug>.html` / `reports/<slug>.html` / `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>` with relative paths only, reusing the same query/templates as the live preview so there's one source of truth, not two. |\n\nNotes on structure:\n- T01 is the only true root; T02/T03/T04 can each start the moment T01's green.\n- T05 split out from T04 rather than folded in, so a file-upload bug can't block the core Report permission model from shipping.\n- T06/T07 both wait on T03+T04 since they read both content types.\n\nTwo questions before I publish:\n1. {"parentUuid":"c813de87-5811-4e0a-b94b-df1209d596e0","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0f469ad3-8e0a-4a2d-83fc-404014162a93","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014D8wg4BqkNmJS9giBoB3NC","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Field notes\n2\t\n3\tI used WordPress Playground to try the same kinds of jobs the Institutional\n4\tResearch office would need to do in this project. I made an Update, a Report\n5\tpage, and a separate account for an intern.\n6\t\n7\t1. The admin dashboard is a lot. I counted 44 links in the main menu before I\n8\t   even started editing anything. WordPress has sections for plugins, themes,\n9\t   media, comments, tools, and a bunch of settings. An IR intern should not have\n10\t   to dig through all of that just to post a deadline or survey Update.\n11\t\n12\t2. Draft and published really are two different states. I saved a post called\n13\t   \"Fall 2026 Survey Update: First Look\" as a draft and could not find it on the\n14\t   public site. As soon as I published it, the post was public. That made the\n15\t   risk feel more real. A half-checked number cannot be allowed to slip from a\n16\t   draft into a public Update.\n17\t\n18\t3. WordPress made the slug automatically:\n19\t   `fall-2026-survey-update-first-look`. It worked, but I can see these getting\n20\t   long when a Report has an official title. I would rather have the CMS make a\n21\t   sensible slug automatically and still let the author shorten it before\n22\t   publishing.\n23\t\n24\t4. I created a page called \"Institutional Research Reports,\" and it showed up\n25\t   in the public navigation. That felt right for Reports because things like the\n26\t   Factbook, Common Data Set, and Survey Policy should have a permanent place.\n27\t   Updates make more sense in a dated list instead of taking over the main menu.\n28\t\n29\t5. The separate intern account worked the way I hoped for Updates. The intern\n30\t   could publish an Update directly, and the content list showed \"Research\n31\t   Intern\" as the author instead of making everything look like it came from a\n32\t   shared office account.\n33\t\n34\t6. WordPress stopped the intern from opening the Users screen. The exact message\n35\t   was, \"Sorry, you are not allowed to list users.\" That is better than only\n36\t   hiding the Users link because the restriction still worked when I went\n37\t   straight to the page.\n38\t\n39\t7. One permission surprised me: the WordPress Editor could still edit the\n40\t   \"Institutional Research Reports\" page. That does not match what I want for\n41\t   this project. Interns should be able to publish routine Updates, but only the\n42\t   Director should be able to edit or publish Reports. We will need to enforce\n43\t   that rule ourselves instead of copying WordPress's Editor role exactly.\n44\t\n45\t8. The content filters were simple and useful. After making a few items, the\n46\t   list showed `All (4)`, `Mine (1)`, `Published (3)`, and `Draft (1)`. \"Mine\"\n47\t   seems especially useful when several interns have accounts and each person\n48\t   wants to find the Update they were working on.\n49\t\n50\t9. The Permalinks screen offered seven choices, including date-based URLs,\n51\t   numeric URLs, post names, and a custom structure. That is more choice than\n52\t   this small CMS needs. A readable title-based slug is enough, and fewer\n53\t   settings would make it harder for someone to accidentally break the URLs.\n54\t"}]},"uuid":"6bb56ba6-c885-49ca-8da9-b0980961e4a9","timestamp":"2026-09-28T20:48:00.579Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/cms-field-notes.md","content":"# Field notes\n\nI used WordPress Playground to try the same kinds of jobs the Institutional\nResearch office would need to do in this project. I made an Update, a Report\npage, and a separate account for an intern.\n\n1. The admin dashboard is a lot. I counted 44 links in the main menu before I\n   even started editing anything. WordPress has sections for plugins, themes,\n   media, comments, tools, and a bunch of settings. An IR intern should not have\n   to dig through all of that just to post a deadline or survey Update.\n\n2. Draft and published really are two different states. I saved a post called\n   \"Fall 2026 Survey Update: First Look\" as a draft and could not find it on the\n   public site. As soon as I published it, the post was public. That made the\n   risk feel more real. A half-checked number cannot be allowed to slip from a\n   draft into a public Update.\n\n3. WordPress made the slug automatically:\n   `fall-2026-survey-update-first-look`. It worked, but I can see these getting\n   long when a Report has an official title. I would rather have the CMS make a\n   sensible slug automatically and still let the author shorten it before\n   publishing.\n\n4. I created a page called \"Institutional Research Reports,\" and it showed up\n   in the public navigation. That felt right for Reports because things like the\n   Factbook, Common Data Set, and Survey Policy should have a permanent place.\n   Updates make more sense in a dated list instead of taking over the main menu.\n\n5. The separate intern account worked the way I hoped for Updates. The intern\n   could publish an Update directly, and the content list showed \"Research\n   Intern\" as the author instead of making everything look like it came from a\n   shared office account.\n\n6. WordPress stopped the intern from opening the Users screen. The exact message\n   was, \"Sorry, you are not allowed to list users.\" That is better than only\n   hiding the Users link because the restriction still worked when I went\n   straight to the page.\n\n7. One permission surprised me: the WordPress Editor could still edit the\n   \"Institutional Research Reports\" page. That does not match what I want for\n   this project. Interns should be able to publish routine Updates, but only the\n   Director should be able to edit or publish Reports. We will need to enforce\n   that rule ourselves instead of copying WordPress's Editor role exactly.\n\n8. The content filters were simple and useful. After making a few items, the\n   list showed `All (4)`, `Mine (1)`, `Published (3)`, and `Draft (1)`. \"Mine\"\n   seems especially useful when several interns have accounts and each person\n   wants to find the Update they were working on.\n\n9. The Permalinks screen offered seven choices, including date-based URLs,\n   numeric URLs, post names, and a custom structure. That is more choice than\n   this small CMS needs. A readable title-based slug is enough, and fewer\n   settings would make it harder for someone to accidentally break the URLs.\n","numLines":54,"startLine":1,"totalLines":54}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c813de87-5811-4e0a-b94b-df1209d596e0","session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"0bb6136a-30a3-428d-b89b-328ce3a93136","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWVjBWCApWgU8bVcFMmT","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KSyVTgicU618msU322a1bP","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md","content":"# Analysts publish Data Bites directly; only the Director publishes Reports; each intern gets their own Analyst account\n\n**Status:** accepted (supersedes an earlier draft of this ADR that proposed one shared Analyst account)\n\nAnalysts (interns) currently email IR staff or drop files in a shared\nOneDrive folder to get anything posted, which is the exact bottleneck this\nCMS exists to remove. But Reports (Factbook, Common Data Set, Survey Policy)\nget cited externally and must stay accurate and stable, so we don't want\nintern turnover or a drafting mistake taking one live unreviewed.\n\nWe decided: the editor permission is split by content type, not uniform.\nAnalysts can create, edit, and **publish** a Data Bite without approval.\nAnalysts can create and edit a Report, but only the Director (admin) can\npublish or edit a Report once it exists — even one an Analyst drafted.\n\n**Accounts:** each intern gets their own named Analyst account, not a shared\nlogin. This reverses an earlier version of this decision. Trying WordPress\nPlayground surfaced the reason: a shared account makes every Data Bite's\nauthor say \"Analyst,\" with no way to tell which intern actually wrote it,\nwhich felt wrong the moment it was compared against a real WordPress content\nlist showing a real name. Individual accounts cost the Director a few extra\nminutes of user management per intern rotation (create/deactivate each\nsemester) — worth it for honest attribution.\n\n**Shift continuity is preserved despite individual accounts:** any Analyst\nmay edit any other Analyst's draft (Data Bite or draft Report), so a\nhalf-finished item from last week's intern doesn't need Director\nintervention to pick back up. Editing preserves the original author and\n`created_at`; only `updated_at` changes. This means \"Analyst\" is a role, not\nan ownership boundary — the boundary that matters is Analyst vs. Director,\nnot Analyst-A vs. Analyst-B.\n\nThe alternative (uniform editor rights, or a Director-approves-everything\ngate) was rejected: the former risks an intern accidentally publishing a\nFactbook revision, the latter reintroduces the \"email IR to post something\"\nbottleneck for the routine, low-stakes case.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1442,"cache_read_input_tokens":152247,"output_tokens":911,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1442,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":911,"cache_read_input_tokens":152247,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1442,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1442},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01KSyVTgicU618msU322a1bP":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md","content":"# Analysts publish Data Bites directly; only the Director publishes Reports; each intern gets their own Analyst account\n\n**Status:** accepted (supersedes an earlier draft of this ADR that proposed one shared Analyst account)\n\nAnalysts (interns) currently email IR staff or drop files in a shared\nOneDrive folder to get anything posted, which is the exact bottleneck this\nCMS exists to remove. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff","originalFile":"# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. A single shared account used by whichever intern is on\nshift that semester — not one account per person. Can draft and publish\nData Bites directly; can draft but not publish or edit Reports.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":13,"oldLines":9,"newStart":13,"newLines":10,"lines":[" _Avoid_: Admin, superuser"," "," **Analyst**:","-The editor role. A single shared account used by whichever intern is on","-shift that semester — not one account per person. The Director\ncan see everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.","originalFile":"# Client brief — Kenyon Office of Institutional Research\n\n**Who runs it, how comfortable are they with computers?** Two people: a\nDirector (modeled on the real office's Associate VP for IR) and\nAnalysts/interns who rotate by semester. Comfortable with spreadsheets and\nWord, not with anything more technical — Markdown with a preview is about the\nceiling.\n\n**Who reads it, what are they after?** Split audience. Internally, faculty\nand administrators come back for the current Factbook and enrollment numbers.\nAccreditors and board members want historical reports for self-studies.\nExternally, some of it — the Factbook, Common Data Set, Data Gallery — is\ngenuinely public, matching what's actually live on kenyon.edu today.\n\n**What's broken now?** Reports live scattered across a shared OneDrive\nfolder with inconsistent naming. Multiple interns work on things at the same\ntime, so it's unclear which version is current, and people end up emailing\nIR directly to ask \"what's the latest Factbook\" instead of finding it\nthemselves.\n\n**What would make them say \"this is better\"?** Whichever intern is on shift\ncan draft and publish a routine Data Bite, under the shared Analyst account,\nwithout emailing a link around or waiting on the Director. The Director can\nsee everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything\nsensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR\nto ask where the latest Factbook is.\n\n**What must never happen?** Draft or unreleased data (e.g. this term's\nstill-being-verified enrollment numbers) must never appear on the public\nsite before it's official. Relatedly, a Report that's already published and\ncited elsewhere (Factbook, CDS) must never be editable or publishable by\nanyone but the Director — see [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-split-publish-rights.md).\nInterns share one Analyst account (a deliberate trade-off, also in ADR-003),\nso this constraint is what actually protects the office, not per-person\naccountability on the low-stakes content.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":19,"oldLines":9,"newStart":19,"newLines":10,"lines":[" themselves."," "," **What would make them say \"this is better\"?** Whichever intern is on shift","-can draft and publish a routine Data Bite, under the shared Analyst account,","-without emailing a link around or waiting on the Director. The Director","+can see everything — drafts and published — in one dashboard before anything"," sensitive goes live. And once something's published, people stop emailing IR"," to ask where the latest Factbook is."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"04e7fdee-b502-41f2-a823-9d1b26e27f98","session_id":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"999d2722-6532-412d-b424-27cb5954f6c3","version":"2.1.283","gitBranch":"main"}
